literal: Those who do not live so that fame arises do not blame themselves; what is the use of blaming those who despise them?
translation: What is the point of blaming those who despise them, when those who fail to live a life of fame do not blame themselves?
modern: புகழ் உண்டாகும்படி வாழாதவர்கள் தம்மைத் தாமே நொந்து கொள்ளாமல், தம்மை இகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்களை நொந்து கொள்வதால் என்ன பயன்?
explanation: This couplet explains that a person who does not live a life worthy of earning fame has only themselves to blame. The word 'tannōvār' (from 'tam' and 'nōvār') shows that such people fail to self-reflect or hold themselves accountable for their lack of reputation. Instead of correcting their own path, they get upset at others who mock or look down on them. The poet asks what possible use there is in blaming others when the root of the problem lies entirely within oneself.
